title: Continual delta scanner: multi-slice rehearse for PR perf gating
creator: Asha Nair
description: Build a continuous delta-scanner harness that runs lightweight, reproducible perf rehearsals in CI for every PR. The harness will: 1) run stratified micro-slices (short, medium, long seq) seeded with realistic prefix traffic and optional synthetic microbursts; 2) measure throughput (tokens/sec) and latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) with per-run bootstrap confidence intervals; 3) compute a delta profile against a rolling canonical baseline using quantile-fusion and bootstrap hypothesis testing (CI overlap + minimum detectable effect guard); 4) apply a gating policy that annotates the PR with PASS/WARN/FAIL and blocks merges on sustained regressions beyond configured thresholds. The design emphasizes low cost per-PR (aim <= 2s GPU-seconds equivalent), reproducibility across hardware (calibration step), and minimizing flakiness via repeat sampling, sample-size checks, and a small randomized control group for variance estimation. Integration points: GitHub PR status checks, Redwood Console perf dashboards (per-model/per-route views), Slack/ops alerts for P0 regressions, and a runbook link for triage. Deliverables: harness code (Go + python runner), CI orb/job templates, dashboard tiles, docs and runbook, a migration script to convert existing canonical baselines to the rolling anchor model.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha Nair: Initial ticket created after perf retro; current pain points: sporadic p95 regressions in PRs, noisy baselines, and expensive full-load benchmarks blocking merges.

2025-02-13 - Marco V.: Spike done - small-scale harness prototype runs locally; bootstrap CIs look stable with 10 repeats per slice. Observed per-slice variance correlates with KV cache warmup pattern.

2025-02-15 - Priya R. (SRE): Recommended adding a hardware-calibration step to normalize tokens/sec across runner types. Also suggested an early-exit when variance is too high to avoid wasting credits.
